summary.headline: The Select Board raised transfer station sticker fees for FY27 and discussed planning a five-year Proposition 2 1/2 operating override for FY28.
summary.summary: The Select Board approved new transfer station rates for fiscal year 2027, raising primary resident stickers to $320 and senior stickers to $75, while postponing revisions to station and swap shop operating rules. Officials examined long-range budget forecasts projecting a $2 million operating deficit in fiscal year 2028 and debated pursuing a multi-year Proposition 2 1/2 override. The board also approved a retail all-alcohol package store license transfer, reviewed the town administrator's annual evaluation, and received updates on regional water negotiations with Hopkinton.

topics.title: Fire department commendations and lifesaving awards
topics.summary: The fire chief presented department unit citations and awards recognizing firefighters for their work on two recent rescue incidents in Southborough. Crew members were commended for a water rescue of a fisherman at a pond off Crystal Pond Road and a technical aerial rescue of an injured worker trapped in a tree on Pinecone Lane.
key_details: A unit citation was awarded to Captain Doan, Captain Amendola, Firefighter Specific, and Firefighter Kipp for the June 7 Crystal Pond Road water rescue.
A unit citation was awarded to Captain Roach, Firefighter Rice, Firefighter Stapleton, Firefighter Kipp, and Firefighter Braccio for the June 11 Pinecone Lane tree rescue.
Firefighter William Kipp received the Firefighter Cross for heroism after ascending a crane harness 60 to 100 feet to secure and lower the injured worker.
topics.outcome: Commendations presented; no board action required.

topics.title: Turnpike Wine and Liquor license transfer and pledge
topics.summary: The board opened a public hearing to consider transferring an annual retail all-alcohol package store license for 65 Turnpike Road to Cabins LLC, doing business as Turnpike Wine and Liquor. Counsel for the applicant confirmed the purchase from Virgin Mary Mother of Light Inc., that the manager has retail liquor experience, and that the business will install ID scanners.
key_details: Applicant Cabins LLC is wholly owned by Monil Patel, with Prateek Patel designated as manager on record.
The applicant also requested approval of a pledge of the liquor license and inventory to lender Rockland Trust.
The license manager will work on-site at least 40 hours per week.
topics.outcome: The board voted 5-0 to approve the license transfer and the pledge to Rockland Trust.

topics.title: FY27 transfer station sticker rates and regulations
topics.summary: The Department of Public Works presented updated regulations and fee options for the transfer station to address operational expenses, including temporary outside hauling costs of $62,000 while town staff obtain commercial driver's licenses. After debating sticker pricing for residents and seniors, the board adopted fee option 2 but postponed proposed rules restricting swap shop drop-offs and large items to August 11.
key_details: Primary non-senior household permits were increased from $295 to $320.
Senior first permits were increased from $50 to $75; second senior permits rose from $15 to $25.
Second permits for non-senior households remained unchanged at $25, and hardship waivers remain available at no cost.
Proposed swap shop restrictions on furniture, baby seats, and sports gear drew board debate and were deferred for refinement.
topics.outcome: The board voted 5-0 to approve the option 2 transfer station sticker fees, while continuing consideration of the operational regulations to August 11.
topics.why_it_matters: Transfer station fees are increasing for all Southborough households using the facility, including a 50 percent increase on senior permits.

topics.title: Hopkinton water connection intermunicipal agreement status
topics.summary: Officials received an update on the proposed intermunicipal agreement to convey MWRA water through Southborough's distribution network to the town of Hopkinton. Negotiations have resumed after stalling in 2023, but Hopkinton requires state approvals, and Southborough must engage an independent engineering firm for design peer review and appoint special counsel due to town counsel representing both municipalities.
key_details: The agreement contemplates Hopkinton reimbursing Southborough for pumping and maintenance costs plus a $1 million payment for local water projects.
Hopkinton will fund curb-to-curb street repaving where roadways are opened for main installation.
Engineering includes replacing the 1930s Oak Hill Road water tank with a taller tank, requiring Zoning Board of Appeals approval.
Town counsel represents both towns, requiring Southborough to hire special municipal counsel to negotiate the final contract terms.
topics.outcome: Update provided; the board will bring forward a vote to appoint special counsel at a future meeting.
topics.why_it_matters: The multi-million-dollar regional water connection could provide Southborough with capital infrastructure upgrades and $1 million in project funding, but will require pipe construction, road repaving, and a new water tank on Oak Hill Road.

topics.title: FY28 budget forecasting and potential Proposition 2 1/2 override
topics.summary: The board began preliminary discussions on the fiscal year 2028 operating budget, reviewing long-range estimates indicating a projected $2 million deficit in FY28 that would exhaust remaining tax levy capacity. Following consultations with state Division of Local Services advisors, the chair outlined a strategy to consider a 5-year operational override to create excess levy capacity rather than returning to voters annually.
key_details: Southborough avoided an override in FY27, maintaining roughly $500,000 in unused levy capacity, but current revenue growth cannot support projected 5 percent annual departmental spending growth and 8 percent benefit increases.

A multi-year operational override approach would ask voters to approve excess levy capacity to fund operations across roughly five years, with property taxes raised only as needed in each annual budget.
Any potential operating override requires both a two-thirds vote at Town Meeting and a majority vote at a town election.
Potential override impacts would run alongside separate upcoming debt exclusion votes for the Neary school building project.
topics.outcome: Discussion held; the board will hold a joint session with the Advisory Committee on August 11 to set the official FY28 budget calendar and guidelines.
topics.why_it_matters: Taxpayers could face a significant Proposition 2 1/2 property tax override vote at Town Meeting and on the ballot in 2027 to prevent substantial municipal and school budget reductions.

topics.title: Town and committee reports
topics.summary: The chair reported on ongoing summer road repaving, the upcoming August agenda item regarding the Stewardship Committee, and confirmation that the town declined its Chapter 61A right of first refusal on Johnson Road. Member Sam Stivers reported that the Wastewater Committee voted to suspend its consulting contract with MassDevelopment to first investigate site suitability and state discharge permitting.
key_details: The Wastewater Committee voted not to proceed with a MassDevelopment financial analysis until soil conditions and DEP discharge limits are evaluated for proposed disposal sites.
The town will not exercise its right of first refusal on the 61A parcel on Johnson Road after the Affordable Housing Trust opted not to purchase.
The town received an authentic replica print of the Declaration of Independence produced by the state 250th committee, which will be framed and displayed in the Town House.

topics.title: Routine business
topics.summary: The board approved several routine items on the consent agenda, including meeting minutes, institutional donations, and a mural installation on a town sign.
key_details: Approved open session minutes for June 16 (with amendments) and June 29.
Accepted annual donations from the New England Center for Children ($105,000 in lieu of taxes) and Fay School ($20,000 for police drone equipment for FY27).
Approved a painted decorative mural on the municipal transfer station sign subject to final visual review.
topics.outcome: The board voted 5-0 to approve consent agenda items A through R.

topics.title: Town administrator performance evaluation and FY27 goals
topics.summary: The board discussed the annual performance review of Town Administrator Mark Purple, awarding a composite numerical rating of 3.59 on a 5-point scale. Board members then established and voted on five primary performance goals for the administrator for fiscal year 2027.
key_details: The administrator received an overall evaluation average of 3.59 out of 5 based on ratings from three eligible board members.

The five adopted FY27 goals are: website redesign and digital communication strategy; implementation of the employee pay and classification study; health insurance cost reduction (including high-deductible plans and OPEB); FY28 budget planning and operational override scenarios; and operationalizing the regional emergency dispatch center transition.
topics.outcome: The board voted 5-0 to approve the five adopted performance goals for the town administrator.

votes.motion: Approve the transfer of the all-alcohol package store license and pledge of license and inventory to Rockland Trust for Cabins LLC d/b/a Turnpike Wine and Liquor at 65 Turnpike Road.

Approve Option 2 for fiscal year 2027 transfer station permit fees ($320 for first non-senior permit, $25 for second non-senior permit, $75 for first senior permit, $25 for second senior permit, and $0 for waived hardship permits).
Approve consent agenda items A through R as presented, including amended minutes of June 16 and acceptance of donations.
Approve the five proposed fiscal year 2027 goals for the town administrator.

public_comment.summary: A resident of North Street and chair of the Stewardship Committee expressed disappointment that the board's agenda omitted discussion of the Stewardship Committee's unanimous recommendations regarding membership and the reappointment of a key volunteer, asking that it be placed on the August agenda.
A resident of Hillside Avenue advocated for keeping the Open Space Preservation Commission and the Stewardship Committee separate and urged the reappointment of their former chair.

A resident of Hillside Avenue urged the board to focus transfer station enforcement on preventing illegal dumping of trash rather than prohibiting residents from reusing furniture and household items at the swap shop.

A resident of Southwood Drive commented on the value of the transfer station swap shop and online freecycle networks, suggesting that the town resolve liability barriers and bring back volunteer oversight rather than overly restricting accepted items.

A resident of Pine Hill Road suggested considering broader consolidation of departmental budgets into large functional areas to improve municipal efficiency and advised framing any override clearly around levy capacity needs.

A resident of Davis Road warned that altering the traditional line-item budget presentation during an override year could raise voter skepticism and noted that Town Meeting can vote on contingent budgets tied to ballot overrides.
